newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu committed to Hebron troop withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu committed to Hebron troop withdrawal.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he was "absolutely committed" to withdraw Israeli troops from Hebron in the West Bank and was ready to conclude an agreement so long as Israeli security was also guaranteed.

"I'm absolutely committed to it," Netanyahu said at a news conference concluding a two-day Middle East crisis summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Jordan's King Hussein and U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington.

Hebron is the last major town on the Palestinian-run West Bank still patrolled by Israeli troops. Israel agreed a year ago to a partial pullback but has since declined to follow through because it seeks guarantees of security against Arab violence.

"We've made it very clear that we are committed to a redeployment in Hebron. We're not reluctant to do it, we're prepared to do it, but in such a way as to avoid a breakdown that would collapse the peace process not only in Hebron but altogether," Netanyahu said.

"And this too will require intensive negotiations. This is perhaps the most important practical thing that we have decided (in Washington): to begin as early as possible, on Sunday, simultaneous negotiations on Hebron and on security and to continue those negotiations until completion."
He said he and Arafat had agreed to intervene personally in the negotiations among their deputies if necessary to reach success.
